title: Automated Urinalysis Analyzer
purpose: Automates reading of urine reagent strips (chemical analysis) and, in combined systems, digital imaging/flow-based classification of urine sediment (microscopic analysis), improving throughput and reducing reader-to-reader variability versus fully manual urinalysis.
operatingPrinciple: Strip-reading analyzers use reflectance photometry to read each reagent pad's color development at its specified time, converting reflected light intensity into a semi-quantitative result for each analyte. Combined chemistry-plus-sediment systems add a second module that images or classifies formed elements (cells, casts, crystals) in unspun or minimally processed urine using digital image analysis or flow cytometry-like principles, flagging results for technologist confirmation rather than fully replacing manual microscopic review.
basicOperation: Run QC material per the laboratory's schedule before releasing patient strip/sediment results.
Ensure adequate, well-mixed, fresh specimen volume per the analyzer's aspiration requirements.
Review analyzer flags for atypical or borderline sediment findings and route to manual microscopic review per the laboratory's rule set.
calibration: Calibrated per manufacturer schedule using certified calibration material; verified through routine QC runs and correlation checks against manual microscopy on a defined schedule or for flagged specimens.
maintenance: Routine cleaning of strip-reading and imaging optics per manufacturer schedule.
Replace strips/reagents before expiration and monitor for lot-to-lot performance shifts.

commonErrors.problem: Discordant chemical vs. sediment finding (e.g. positive blood chemically, few red cells on sediment)
commonErrors.cause: Hemoglobin/myoglobin present without intact red cells, or a timing/interference issue on the strip pad
commonErrors.fix: Correlate both results and review manually rather than reporting either component in isolation

commonErrors.problem: Sediment classification flag on an atypical element
commonErrors.cause: An element outside the analyzer's trained classification categories (e.g. an unusual crystal or organism)
commonErrors.fix: Route to manual microscopic examination for technologist identification

safety: Treat urine specimens and analyzer waste as biohazardous.
Follow manufacturer decontamination procedures for any maintenance involving fluidics access.
